access_note: The Figshare public API lists a 1.61 MB ZIP for the article-specific 22-event release. The broader NASA COOLR Viewer is a separate access route and collection. No archive was downloaded.
description: NASA researchers published event-based landslide inventories for 22 rainfall events around the world from 2019 to 2023. Their Figshare version-one deposit contains a 1.61 MB ZIP of new event inventories; the article also explains how they join the broader COOLR collection and NASA Landslide Viewer. The article describes shapefile, CSV and geodatabase routes. The deposit is public, free and CC BY 4.0. Hazard and transport simulations can use these mapped events to train or check landslide detection, compare exposed road corridors or assess rainfall-linked disruption. An important limitation is that most points were mapped from roughly 3 m optical imagery, so small slides may be missed. Cloud, shadow, vegetation and the choice of event boundary also affect completeness. The authors caution that the 22 events are not representative of global trends; they did not field-verify every inventory. The ZIP contents were not examined. The catalogue US Landslide Exposure Database is a related national exposure resource, not this multi-event global training sample.
